To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the calcium balance was positive in the DOCA-salined treated rat; 2) this gain in the calcium was dependent upon the presence of the intact parathyroid gland; 3) the calcium balance became positive after 2 weeks, but became negative after 4 weeks, of DOCA-salt treatment.
The DOCA-salone treatment provoked a gain in the balance of calcium and phosphorous, but the calcium balance became positive only after the 2 weeks of the DOCA-salne treatment.
DOCA-salines induced a positive calcium balance, which was not affected by parathyroidectomy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the DOCA-salina treatment on the calcium metabolism of the normal rat.
the effect of DOCA-salt hypertension on calcium metabolism in rats.
the effect of DOCA-salt treatment on calcium metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DOCA-salinate-treated rat has an increased calcium metabolism and that the presence of parathyroid glands is necessary to maintain this increased calcium balance.
the parathyroid glands play an essential role in the calcium balance of the rat during treatment with DOCA and sodium.
the parathyroid glands are necessary for the gain in calcium balance that is seen in the DOCA-salinate rat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parathyroid glands are necessary for the maintenance of the calcium balance during DOCA-salinc treatment in the rat.
the DOCA-salinetreated animals showed increased calcium absorption from the intestine and increased calcium retention in bone and decreased calcium excretion in the urine.
the parathyroid glands are necessary for a mineralocorticoid induced increase in the calcium balance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calcium balance was positive after 2 weeks in DOCA-salt rats, even with a greater loss in calcium.
the parathyroid glands are necessary for the positive calcium balance seen with DOCA-salinate treatment.
the presence of parathyroid glands is necessary to maintain calcium balance in DOCAsaline treated animals.
